# Define models in a dummy app
class Item(models.Model):
    uid = models.AutoField(primary_key=True, editable=False)
    f = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    
    class Meta:
        app_label = 'reproduce_app'

    def reset(self):
        self.uid = None
        self.f = False

class Derived(Item):
    class Meta:
        app_label = 'reproduce_app'

# Create the tables

with connection.schema_editor() as schema_editor:
    schema_editor.create_model(Item)
    schema_editor.create_model(Derived)

class SaveTestCase(TestCase):

        derived = Derived.objects.create(f=True) # create the first object
        pk = derived.pk
        print(f"Created Derived with pk={pk}, f={derived.f}")
        
        item = Item.objects.get(pk=pk)
        obj1 = item.derived
        print(f"Before reset: obj1.pk={obj1.pk}, obj1.f={obj1.f}")
        obj1.reset()
        print(f"After reset: obj1.pk={obj1.pk}, obj1.f={obj1.f}")
        obj1.save() # the first object is supposed to be overwritten
        
        obj = Item.objects.get(pk=pk)
        print(f"After save: obj.pk={obj.pk}, obj.f={obj.f}")
        self.assertTrue(obj.f, "obj.f should be True if it was overwritten with f=False? Wait, the PR says 'the first object is overwritten' and then tests 'self.assertTrue(obj.f)'. Let me re-read.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    from django.core.management import call_command
    import unittest
    
    # Run the test
    suite = unittest.TestLoader().loadTestsFromTestCase(SaveTestCase)
    unittest.TextTestRunner().run(suite)
